title: Finite-Time Optomechanical Cooling by Multi-Exceptional-Point Braiding
summary: Cooling a mechanical mode in finite time is a routing problem: excitation must reach a lossy mode before thermal noise rebuilds the population. Exceptional points are non-Hermitian degeneracies at which two hybrid modes and their eigenvectors merge, so a loop around them can exchange connected spectral branches. The main obstacle in testing whether this topology improves cooling is causal. Independently optimized enclosing and non-enclosing protocols normally have different waveforms, so topology and waveform geometry change together.
